title: Classic DP problems
description:
```cpp
struct Item { int weight; int value; };

std::pair<int, std::vector<int>> knapsack(const std::vector<Item>& items, int capacity);   // best value and the chosen item indexes (ascending)
std::string lcs(const std::string& a, const std::string& b);                                // one longest common subsequence
int editDistance(const std::string& a, const std::string& b);
int lisLength(const std::vector<int>& values);                                              // strictly increasing; O(n log n)
std::vector<int> lis(const std::vector<int>& values);                                       // one longest increasing subsequence
```

- `knapsack`: 0/1 knapsack (each item at most once). Return the best total value and the indexes of one optimal choice. If several choices are optimal, any is accepted.
- `lcs` may return any longest common subsequence; the tests check that it is common to both strings and has the right length.
- `editDistance` uses insertions, deletions and substitutions, each costing 1, and only O(|b|) memory: the tests compare strings of 5,000 characters.
- `lisLength` must be O(n log n) (the tests use 200,000 values). `lis` returns an actual subsequence (any one of the longest), which needs a parent index for each element.
hints: To rebuild a longest increasing subsequence, remember for each length `k + 1` the **index** of the element currently ending it (`tailIndex[k]`), and for each element the index of the element before it (`parent[i] = tailIndex[k - 1]` at the moment it is placed). Follow parents back from the last tail.
Edit distance with two rows: `prev` is row `i - 1`, `cur` is row `i`. `cur[0] = i`, then fill left to right, and swap the vectors at the end of each row.
